project.title: Why Does Ice Float?
project.visual_style: clean educational 3D infographic; a floating ice cube, liquid-water molecule cluster, open ice lattice, high-contrast labels; no external assets

lesson.learning_goal: Explain that hydrogen bonds arrange frozen water molecules farther apart, making ice less dense than liquid water so it floats.
lesson.source_note: OpenStax Biology 2e, section 2.2: hydrogen bonds form a crystalline structure in ice; molecules are farther apart than in liquid water, so ice is less dense and floats.

narration_beats.text: Most substances get denser when they freeze. Water is a surprising exception.
In liquid water, molecules move around as hydrogen bonds form and break.
As water freezes, hydrogen bonds hold molecules in an open crystal structure.
That structure takes up more space, making ice less dense than liquid water.
So ice floats. On lakes, surface ice can also insulate the water below.
